newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Shock rate hike hits UK stocks, helps pound.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Shock rate hike hits UK stocks, helps pound.

text.p: A shock increase in British interest rates on Wednesday caused a sharp drop in London stocks and sent the pound surging to a 22-month high against the mark.

The rate hike also took a little shine off other European bourses, already nervous about interest rates, although figures showing weaker U.S. growth calmed some of jitters about the pace of inflation in the powerful American economy.

London's bourse, which had registered gains with the rest of Europe in early trading, dropped within minutes of news flashing on dealers screens that the Bank of England was raising the minimum lending rate by a quarter-point to six percent.
British finance minister Kenneth Clarke surprise move wrong-footed financial markets which had predicted he would not risk such a bold move ahead of a general election.
The central bank had been pressing since June for a tightening in monetary policy, arguing that rising economic growth meant there was a risk of a resurgence in inflation within the next two years.
"The strength of activity indicates that a rise in rates is desirable if we are to deliver our inflation target of 2.5 percent or less in the medium term," Clarke said.
London's FTSE index quickly reversed its earlier gains and had fallen by 0.9 percent by mid-afternnon as investors digested the impact of increased rates on corporate profits.

But some traders took a positive view. "We think domestic investors will deem this a very prudent move which will probably put off any more drastic tightening in the future. We are still positive on this market," a senior trader said.

Paris and Frankfurt put on a mixed reaction to the interest rate developments and ahead of important clues on the health of the American economy which may appear in U.S. employment statistics on Friday.
German shares climbed at first, encouraged by firmer German bonds and a strong close on Wall Street overnight but slipped back to show only a modest gain at the finish.
But trading on Frakfurt's after-hours IBID index fell by 0.5 percent as German bonds lost some sheen following the surprise raising of the British rate.
In Paris, stocks climbed after U.S. figures were issued showing weaker consumer spending on new cars and other goods slowed the economy's growth sharply during the third quarter.
But they slid into the minus column after Wall Street made on unsteady opening later in the day.
On currency markets, the pound, buoyant over the past month, benefited from the Bank of England's move giving sterling a better return for investors.
Sterling surged over a pfennig to 2.4615 marks, a 22-month peak against the mark and climbed to 1.6323 dollars, a 19-month high.
"It's been quite a day, and sterling was the prime mover," said Pat Magill, head of the corporate desk at Daiwa Europe in London. "There have been some large trades, " he added.
The dollar, whose recent strength against the yen has taken it to 42-month highs, came under pressure against the yen on Wednesday, dragged down by heavy selling.

The U.S. currency weakened half a yen to 113.85 by mid-afternoon with heavy selling of dollars for yen. The yen's revival had started with sales of Australian dollars for yen in the upper 90s region, dealers said.
CURRENCIES AT 1600 GMT
The dollar was trading around 1.5095 marks and 114.85 yen versus 1.5100 and 114.26 in late European business on Tuesday.
STOCKS AT 1600 GMT
London's FTSE 100 index was down 31.4 points at 3962.1.
Germany's DAX index closed 5.11 higher at 2,678.73.
In Paris, the CAC 40 index was down 0.98 at 2124.76.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $379.70 an ounce in the afternoon, compared to London's Tuesday close of $381.50. Silver was also weaker at $4.82, down three cents.
